title: Conditional Expressions (Ternary)
objective: Write a one-line if-else using a conditional expression.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Full Course for free
sourceAlignment.creator: Bro Code
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only; this topic isn't covered in Python Crash Course but is taught in the companion video. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A conditional expression is a one-line shortcut for a simple if-else that only ever produces a value — no separate blocks, no colons, no indentation. The pattern is value_if_true if condition else value_if_false, read almost like a sentence: return this if the condition holds, otherwise return that.

Because a conditional expression evaluates to a single value, you can print it directly, store it in a variable, or use it anywhere else an if-else would otherwise force you to write several lines. status = "adult" if age >= 18 else "child" does the same job as a four-line if-else block.

Reach for a conditional expression when both outcomes are simple values and the choice itself is the whole point. If either branch needs more than one line of logic, a regular if-else is clearer — don't force a conditional expression just to save space.
explanation.rule: value_if_true if condition else value_if_false evaluates to one of two values in a single expression — a shortcut for a simple if-else, not a replacement for every one.

examples.title: Positive or Negative
examples.code:
num = -5
result = "positive" if num > 0 else "negative"
print(result)
examples.note: num > 0 is False, so result becomes 'negative' — the same outcome as a four-line if-else, in one line.

examples.title: Using It Directly in a print()
examples.note: No variable needed — the conditional expression's result is passed straight into print().

checks.question: num = 4; result = "even" if num % 2 == 0 else "odd" — what is result?

feedback.correct: Correct — num % 2 == 0 is True for 4, so result becomes 'even'.
feedback.incorrect: Check the condition first: num % 2 == 0 is True whenever num is even.

assignment.title: Access Level
assignment.brief: Write access_level(role) that returns 'full access' if role is 'admin', otherwise 'limited access' — using a conditional expression, not an if statement.
requirements: Use a conditional expression (value if condition else value) on the return line.
Do not use a separate if: block.
assignment.starterCode:
def access_level(role):
    # Return 'full access' if role == 'admin' else 'limited access', using a conditional expression.
    pass

print(access_level("admin"))
print(access_level("guest"))
assignment.solutionCode:
def access_level(role):
    return "full access" if role == "admin" else "limited access"

print(access_level("admin"))
print(access_level("guest"))

requirementChecks.label: Does not use an if: block

assignment.testHarness:

assignment.outputCheckLabel: access_level('admin') and access_level('guest') print full access then limited access

hints: The pattern is: return value_if_true if condition else value_if_false.
No if: block is needed — this all fits on one return line.
access_level('guest') should return 'limited access' since 'guest' isn't 'admin'.
